ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a toy car moving along a horizontal line. The labeled positions and times are: Start at 0 s, 6 cm at 0.1 s, 24 cm at 0.2 s, 54 cm at 0.3 s, and 96 cm at 0.4 s. Reasoning: The cart starts from rest and accelerates uniformly, so its displacement from the start follows x = (1/2)at^2. At the 96 cm mark, x = 0.96 m and t = 0.4 s. Solving for acceleration gives a = 2x/t^2 = 2(0.96)/(0.4)^2 = 1.92/0.16 = 12 m/s^2. The instantaneous velocity at that time is v = at = 12(0.4) = 4.8 m/s.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: the cart is at 96 cm from the start at 0.4 s. From the text, note that it starts from rest and accelerates uniformly. For uniform acceleration, the average velocity over the interval from rest to time t equals the mean of initial and final velocities: v_avg = (0 + v)/2. The average velocity from the image data is displacement/time = 96 cm / 0.4 s = 240 cm/s = 2.4 m/s. Therefore the instantaneous velocity at 0.4 s is twice the average velocity, v = 2v_avg = 4.8 m/s.
